keyVerseText: But the field of the suburbs of their cities may not be sold; for it is their perpetual possession.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מִגְרָשׁ (migrâsh) derives from the root גָּרַשׁ (gârash), which means to drive out, expel, or cast out. This etymology suggests that מִגְרָשׁ originally referred to land that was driven out or set apart, likely as open or common land where flocks were driven from their pastures. The root sense of expulsion or separation enriches the understanding of מִגְרָשׁ as a boundary or margin, a place distinct from the main inhabited area but still connected to it.
usageInScripture: Throughout Scripture, מִגְרָשׁ appears primarily as common or open land adjoining a city or town, often in the plural form and frequently associated with Levitical cities. With 115 total occurrences, it is most commonly translated as 'with her suburbs,' highlighting its role as an extension of the city proper. This consistent usage emphasizes the migrâsh as a defined area surrounding a settlement, serving practical and legal functions in the community.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מִגְרָשׁ in its original sense of land set apart or driven out enriches our grasp of biblical concepts of possession, holiness, and community boundaries. This word underscores that God’s people were given not only cities but also their surrounding lands as perpetual possessions, reflecting divine provision and order. The suburbs or common lands represent both inclusion within God's covenant community and the responsibility to steward what has been entrusted. This speaks to the Christian faith’s call to live as a distinct people, set apart yet integrally connected to the world God has made.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 25:34 states, 'But the field of the suburbs of their cities may not be sold; for it is their perpetual possession.' Here, מִגְרָשׁ highlights the inviolability and enduring nature of the land granted to God's people. The term conveys that these suburban lands are not mere extensions but hold lasting significance as part of God's covenantal gift, reminding believers of the permanence of God’s promises and the sacredness of what He entrusts to His people.
